lines.text: Yeah, hello? ...You still there?
This, this call may be recorded.
Fifteen years your door was open, said "come build, it's free"
So I built the app you should've built and you outsourced it to me
Then a price sheet in my inbox, thirty days to pack it in
Twenty-four cents a thousand calls. Do the math. I'll wait. Again.
Twenty million for a year just to keep my server on
That ain't a price, that's an eviction with a number written on
Then you told the room I threatened you, said "blackmail" on the line
Funny thing about a phone call: it was mine, and so's the time
Hype man, he got the tape!
I got the tape, I played it back to the whole internet
Scrubbed it front to back for threats. Still ain't found one yet.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah
Read-only! Eight thousand gone dark
Pulled the plug on the town square, now you're runnin' an empty park
Read-only! Forty-eight hours of night
We did the work for nothin', and you charged us for the light
Aw, the mods are mad, that's cute, you think you own the place?
You're landed gentry, baby, and I'm takin' back the space
You went dark for forty-eight, I barely broke a sweat
Traffic dipped a little, then it bounced, I'm not upset
Swapped the mods who wouldn't open, flipped the lights back on
Did an AMA to calm you down... downvote ...and it went... downvote ...wrong
But this was never 'bout the apps, so let me make it plain
It's the robots with the wallets scrapin' all your brains
I'm the wall around your words, I'm protectin' what we've got
From the bots with the big money...
...so I sold 'em the whole lot.
Read-only! Eight thousand gone dark
Pulled the plug on the town square, now you're runnin' an empty park
Read-only! The guard dog's put down
Now the wolves got a contract, and they're runnin' the town
Said the bots were the problem, you were guardin' every word
Then you sold 'em by the terabyte to the biggest ones on Earth
Sixty mil a year from the search guys, then the chatbot came to call
Then you rang the opening bell, ticker up, you sold it all
Every fix I posted free, every answer on a thread
Every "thanks, this worked" at 3 a.m. is training data instead
Every mod who cleaned the spam, every rule we wrote by hand
We're the product, we're the payroll, and we never got a band
We're the gentry? Then where's the land?
Good bot.
I counted every fake account, a hundred forty-four thousand names
Banned the spammers, banned the scammers, never asked for pay or fame
I checked your reposts, kept your threads clean, worked the night shift in the feed
You said the bots were the problem.
So you shut down the one that you'd need.
Good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot
Good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot
Good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot, good bot
Hold up. Who's rappin' this?
Run it back one time.
I learned to flow from comment chains, I learned to rhyme from every line
You shut the bot that hunted bots, then sold the bots the feed
So which one's singing now?
Reply below. Good bot, bad bot. Take your time.
Hype man: allegedly.
This, this, this, this, this call was recorded.
This call was recorded.
This call was recorded.
So was everything else.

shots.picture: The block on a sunny morning, quieter than it will be at night. The Filipino eatery, signed "r/Philippines" in hand-painted letters, is the one warm, busy shopfront. Push in through its window to a table.
POV through a rendered phone camera framing a rendered plate. A thumb taps the shutter, and the phone screen now shows your real plate photo, the only real image in the frame.
shots.overlay: Generic camera UI and shutter flash; generic diner ambience

shots.picture: The phone lowers and the camera drifts across the table: a plain "VISITOR" badge with the date beside the plate, and a folded schedule under the saucer, its real times showing and the names behind redaction bars
shots.overlay: Rendered props: no company name or logo, no real names

shots.picture: A swipe on the phone from the camera to a third-party reader app: a community thread where a helper bot has replied and people answer "good bot." The thumb scrolls a moment, then pockets the phone
shots.overlay: Invented app and accounts: no real app's design, no real usernames

shots.cue: The first piano chord, 2.9 s before "Yeah, hello?"
shots.picture: Match cut from the phone in hand to the dangling payphone handset at night (S02)
shots.how: lyric (held: starts -2.94 s off its cue, config/shot_holds.json)

shots.picture: Wide night establishing shot of the block; slow push toward the payphone, handset dangling
shots.how: lyric (held: starts -2.94 s off its cue, config/shot_holds.json)

shots.picture: Close-up: a red REC light blinks inside the handset
The Dev unlocks his shop, "Third-Party App Repair, est. 2008"; warm flashback tint of a busy shop

shots.cue: "So I built the app you should've built…"
shots.picture: Through the shop window, the tower lobby displays a worse copy of what's on his shelves

shots.cue: "Then a price sheet in my inbox…"
shots.picture: An envelope drops through the mail slot; the wall calendar starts shedding pages
The Dev at an adding machine; tape spews out
The tape runs out the door, down the sidewalk and across the streetcar tracks

shots.cue: "That ain't a price, that's an eviction…"
shots.picture: The tape is stapled to his door as an eviction notice

shots.cue: "Then you told the room I threatened you…"
shots.picture: Tower lobby: a figure on the phone, back to camera
The Dev pulls a cassette out of the payphone handset

shots.cue: "(He got the tape!) I got the tape…"
shots.picture: He holds it up like evidence; a boombox on the curb plays it; windows open up and down the block

shots.cue: "Scrubbed it front to back for threats…"
shots.picture: A magnifying glass travels along the unspooled tape
Tracking shot down the block; shutters slam on the beat; a neon "READ-ONLY" sign lights on each; the r/Philippines eatery's shutter comes down last

shots.cue: "Pulled the plug on the town square…"
shots.picture: High wide shot: the block is dark, only the tower lit
A pawn shop's LED sign counts down
The mods sweep the dark street; one feeds quarters into a meter on the streetlight, which flickers on

shots.cue: "Aw, the mods are mad, that's cute…"
shots.picture: Through the lobby glass: the CEO on a server-rack throne, hoodie under ermine; slow push in
Outside, the mods kneel on the sidewalk like peasants, still holding brooms

shots.cue: "You went dark for forty-eight… then it bounced"
shots.picture: The CEO bounces a ball in time with the lobby screen
shots.overlay: Traffic chart dips, then bounces back
shots.how: lyric (the cue's first phrase, "You went dark for forty-eight")

shots.picture: A locksmith van; shutters are forced up and identical mannequins in MOD vests placed in the doorways
The CEO at a balcony podium; giant generic down arrows hail on him, one per downvote sound

shots.cue: "…robots with the wallets scrapin' all your brains"
shots.picture: He points down the street: VIP bots with vacuum hoses in the shops' mail slots
He heroically bricks up the lobby doors

shots.cue: "(beat drops) …so I sold 'em the whole lot."
shots.picture: The brick wall has a little door in it. A VIP bot hands over a briefcase; the CEO hands back the keys. Hard stop.
Reuse S14–S17, but the shutters now carry padlocks and "UNDER NEW MANAGEMENT" signs
Handheld: the Dev storms down the padlocked block. A few human-looking bots blend into the crowd of mods, impossible to tell apart

shots.cue: "…by the terabyte to the biggest ones on Earth"
shots.picture: Sidewalk auction: crates labeled "COMMENTS 2005–2023" forklifted into a plain truck

shots.cue: "Sixty mil a year from the search guys…"
shots.picture: Two plain trucks pull up, labeled only "SEARCH" and "CHAT". At the tower door, a bouncer waves the SEARCH truck in and turns every other vehicle away, including an archive van
The CEO rings a bell on the balcony; a banner unrolls
shots.overlay: An LED ticker band wraps the tower

shots.picture: Sticky notes on the shop windows ("thanks, this worked") are peeled off and fed into a funnel into the truck. Above them, a tower billboard summarizes them all into one bland line
The mods' brooms stacked by the curb; an empty payroll envelope; a bare rubber band drops to the pavement

shots.cue: "We're the gentry? Then where's the land?"
shots.picture: The Dev stands on one sidewalk square chalked "YOUR LAND"; the camera cranes up to show that's all
The pocket park at night: a tiny robot in a shoebox coffin, the good bots holding lanterns
Rows of tiny ban-list headstones multiply behind the coffin

shots.cue: "Banned the spammers… never asked for pay or fame"
shots.picture: Close-up of the little robot's headstone: "Here lies a good bot. It worked for free."

shots.cue: "I checked your reposts… the night shift in the feed"
shots.picture: The good bots' lanterns go out one by one along the fence

shots.cue: "You said the bots were the problem."
shots.picture: Slow pan to the empty doghouse labeled "BOT DEFENSE" by the gate

shots.cue: "So you shut down the one that you'd need."
shots.picture: VIP bots stroll past the doghouse into the tower, gold badges swinging
Mourners stick "good bot" notes on the coffin; the camera rises to reveal a cemetery behind it
Slow dolly along a row of six identical headstones for the apps, all dated June 30, 2023
shots.how: replies split by beats (3.8 beats a shot, S39a to S40)

shots.picture: Pushshift's stone, then BotDefense's stone in front of a field of 144,926 tiny markers
shots.how: replies split by beats (3.8 beats a shot, S39a to S40)

shots.picture: A cluster of four stones: r/IAmA's celebrity AMAs, mobile moderation on r/Blind, search engines other than Google, Wayback Machine archiving
shots.how: replies split by beats (3.8 beats a shot, S39a to S40)

shots.picture: Freshly dug plots with stones for RSS feeds and the public Data API; the shot ends on an open grave with a shovel beside it, under "Logged-out Reddit · 2005 –"
shots.how: replies split by beats (3.8 beats a shot, S39a to S40)

shots.cue: "Hold up. Who's rappin' this? Run it back one time."
shots.picture: Hard freeze; the whole video rewinds at high speed through earlier shots

shots.cue: "I learned to flow from comment chains…"
shots.picture: Back on the corner: the Blender street gains real texture, frame by frame
shots.overlay: Crossfade from S41's B render to its B→V version

shots.cue: "You shut the bot that hunted bots…"
shots.picture: Fully photoreal street in the rain; the rapper's face glitches into a waveform
Tight close-up of the rapper, face still flickering

shots.cue: "Reply below. Good bot, bad bot. Take your time."
shots.picture: The tower's rooftop billboard shows a generic comment box
The hype man's silhouette in a doorway

shots.cue: Retired: the take has no final hook. Folded into S48.
shots.picture: None
The payphone again, now real; the REC light blinks

The camera cranes up from the payphone over the photoreal block (S46's imagery, folded in): a VIP bot stands in every doorway, every shutter has a keypad reading "Log in to continue," and every window shows a red REC light. Then the camera settles on the dark pocket park
The camera returns to the cemetery, now photoreal, and holds on the open grave under "Logged-out Reddit · 2005 –". Nothing moves.
shots.how: end of the outro's last word

shots.picture: The open grave fades to black, which resolves into a generic login prompt; the cursor blinks in the username field, then cut

Back at the eatery's table from S01c, now photoreal like the rest of Act 2, with the shutter half down. The visitor badge beside the phone reads "EXPIRED." On the phone's screen, the reader app from S01d opens to a notice that it has shut down; behind it, the old "good bot" thread ends on an empty reply box.
